title: Ancient Timeline
description: A scrubbable timeline of South Asian history from about 7000 BCE (Mehrgarh) to about 550 CE (the end of the Gupta Empire), linked to a schematic map. As the year changes, eleven places across Pakistan, Afghanistan, India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka light up and an event card explains what was happening.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Ancient history
South Asia
Indus Valley Civilization
Maurya and Gupta empires
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Put the major ancient periods of South Asia in order, from Mehrgarh to the Gupta Empire.
Connect each period to the places where it happened and to the present-day countries those places are in.
Recognize that some periods overlapped, such as the Kushan Empire in the north and the Sangam Age in the Tamil south.
prerequisites: Reading BCE and CE dates (bigger BCE numbers are older)
The Indus and Ganga rivers and the Indo-Gangetic Plain from Chapter 1
keyQuestions: Which came first: the Indus cities, the Vedas or the Buddha?
Which ancient sites are in Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka rather than India?
Which powers existed at the same time around 100 CE?
misconceptions: South Asian history begins with the Vedas.
Ancient South Asian history happened only in present-day India.
One empire always ruled the whole region at a time.
controls: Click or tap a dot on the map
dataSources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre listings for Moenjodaro, Taxila, Lumbini, Anuradhapura and Nalanda: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/
